slot.brief: Two projectiles fired with complementary angles with same speed; compare their ranges, maximum heights and times of flight qualitatively.

stem: Two projectiles are launched from level ground with equal speeds, one at $62^\circ$ and the other at $28^\circ$ to the horizontal. If their ranges, maximum heights and flight times are $R_A,H_A,T_A$ and $R_B,H_B,T_B$, respectively, which comparison is correct?

verdicts.working: For launch angle θ, R = u²sin(2θ)/g, H = u²sin²θ/(2g), and T = 2usinθ/g. Since 62° and 28° are complementary, ranges are equal; 62° gives greater height and flight time.

working:
$R=\dfrac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$; $\sin 124^\circ=\sin 56^\circ\Rightarrow R_A=R_B$.
$H=\dfrac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$; $\sin 62^\circ>\sin 28^\circ\Rightarrow H_A>H_B$.
$T=\dfrac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$; $\sin 62^\circ>\sin 28^\circ\Rightarrow T_A>T_B$.

Independent check: For launch angle θ, R = u²sin(2θ)/g, H = u²sin²θ/(2g), and T = 2usinθ/g. Since 62° and 28° are complementary, ranges are equal; 62° gives greater height and flight time.

draft.stem: Two projectiles are launched from level ground with equal speeds, one at $62^\circ$ and the other at $28^\circ$ to the horizontal. If their ranges, maximum heights and flight times are $R_A,H_A,T_A$ and $R_B,H_B,T_B$, respectively, which comparison is correct?
draft.distractor_notes:
B: reverses the height and time comparisons by interchanging the angle effects.
C: incorrectly assumes the larger launch angle gives a larger range.
D: reverses the time-of-flight comparison.
